newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says plans to privatise DSL Bank.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says plans to privatise DSL Bank.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry on Thursday said it planned to privatise the state-controlled Deutsche Siedlungs und Landesrentenbank, or DSL Bank, but said it had not yet identified a buyer for the bank.
A Finance Ministry spokeswoman, responding to a Reuter inquiry, said there had been no definite decision on how to privatise DSL.
"A sale to Postbank is a possible option," she said.

Postbank, the postal bank due for privatisation next year, said on Wednesday it had been discussing cooperation with DSL for some time. But Postbank refused to confirm or deny talk that it was poised for an outright takeover of DSL.

Speculation about a takeover by Postbank was heightened by the news on Wednesday that BHW, the diversified financial group with an interest in closer links with Postbank, had cut its stake in DSL to above 10 percent from more than 20 percent.
The Wirtschaftswoche magazine said on Thursday that Postbank's takeover plans for DSL were well advanced.
The government owns 51.5 percent of DSL while the states of Bavaria and Berlin together own another 0.5 percent.

DSL said in May that it was satisfied with its majority state ownership although it was aiming for full privatisation in due course. Chairman Stefan Juette said at the time that DSL was "not at the top" of the privatisation list.

DSL, active in underwriting business, achieved a 30 percent increase in its balance sheet total to 102.1 billion marks in 1996 and its operating profit after risk provisions rose 24 percent to 123.1 million marks.
